subject: Private VPC: 'Tether Meshlet' topology and cross-plane alignment review
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Nexa Cloud Ops <nexa-ops@nexacloud.com>
Cc: OnSite Networking <ops@on-site.io>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC: 'Tether Meshlet' topology and cross-plane alignment review

Team / Nexa-ops —

Attaching the first-pass topology and control/data mapping for the "Tether Meshlet" private VPC deployment we're proposing for the NexaCloud pilot. This is intentionally compact: a cluster of small "meshlet" pods at customer edge sites that federate back to a regional control plane and a shared data-plane KV/proxy fabric.

High-level asks:
- Can infra confirm the control-plane demarc (TLS, cert propagation, control API endpoints) is acceptable for a multi-tenant meshlet footprint?
- Ops: validate the proposed KV proxy pattern (sidecar vs dedicated proxy) for large inference KV cache reuse across tenants — see mapping sheet attached.
- Networking: egress constraints — we propose a single egress relay per meshlet with enforced NAT and prefix-allowlist; need Nexa to confirm allowed outbound ranges.

What I've attached:
- tether-meshlet-diagram.png (simple topology + cross-plane labels)
- controlplane-data-mapping.xlsx (mapping of services, ports, cert flows and observability hooks)

Notes / assumptions:
- Meshlets run in customer colos with minimal NAT — we rely on mTLS to the regional control plane and an L7 relay for telemetry.
- KV cache warmers are allowed to fetch from the regional fabric; we built a fallback to a smaller local cache for network partitions.

Concrete questions for this thread so we can converge before Thursday's architecture review:
1) Is the sidecar approach safe for KV throughput, or do we need a dedicated proxy process per meshlet? (impact: latency and GPU op density)
2) Are there minimum MTU/overlay constraints we should call out for the colos?
3) Any objections to routing telemetry via the control plane relay vs direct ingestion?

Thanks — please add quick inline comments to the diagram or reply. If helpful I can run a 30m call to walk through the flows.

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Nexa Cloud Ops <nexa-ops@nexacloud.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 11:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC: 'Tether Meshlet' topology and cross-plane alignment review

Kimberly — thanks for the clear framing and attachments. Quick read-through notes below (inline):

> - Can infra confirm the control-plane demarc (TLS, cert propagation, control API endpoints) is acceptable for a multi-tenant meshlet footprint?

- Short answer: yes, provided we bake certificate rotation into the control-plane agent and avoid relying solely on long-lived node certs. We should define token exchange flows for short-lived cert issuance (10-30m TTL) and record audit events for issuance/renewal.

> - Ops: validate the proposed KV proxy pattern (sidecar vs dedicated proxy) for large inference KV cache reuse across tenants — see mapping sheet attached.

- Recommendation: start with sidecar for ease of deployment and isolation, but allow an operator-mode that collapses to a dedicated proxy when throughput > X ops/s (we should define X after perf runs). Sidecar helps with fault isolation and makes canarying safer.

> - Egress constraints — we propose a single egress relay per meshlet with enforced NAT and prefix-allowlist; need Nexa to confirm allowed outbound ranges.

- Agree on a single egress relay per meshlet. Practical constraints: if customers require strict whitelisting, we'll need to publish a small IP set (or use egress FQDNs) and include a port table in the runbook.

Other items:
- MTU: require 1500 path or clear fallback for overlay fragmentation. Add a simple MTU check in the agent preflight.
- Observability: prefer telemetry forked at the relay (lighter touch) and a sampling policy for tokenized requests to avoid high cardinality logs.

I'll add comments directly into the mapping sheet with suggested TTLs and a proposed sidecar/dedicated switch threshold.

Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Infra Engineer, Runtime
irene_choi@redwood.ai
(attachment: controlplane-data-mapping.xlsx - annotated)

Subject: Private VPC: 'Tether Meshlet' topology and cross-plane alignment review
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Adding a quick diagram iteration (attached) with three variations:
A) Sidecar-first (single proxy per workload)
B) Dedicated proxy per meshlet (shared across workloads)
C) Hybrid (sidecar by default, operator collapses proxies during high load)

I called out the following in the PNG:
- Control-plane API endpoints (two regional endpoints for active/standby)
- Preferred certificate rotation window (15m default)
- Observability ingress points (relay vs direct)

Requests from my side:
- Jonas: can you confirm the failover path for regional control-plane if active endpoint loses reachability? We should ensure meshlets prefer standby only after X successive failures to avoid split-brain.
- Nexa Ops: please confirm outbound IP ranges for the egress relay and whether FQDN-based allowlisting is acceptable.

If we agree on the hybrid pattern (C), it reduces operator burden for early pilots and gives us a clear escalation path to switch to B when we measure load.

I propose a 30m sync tomorrow to lock down the runbook and acceptance criteria (preflight checks: MTU, cert issuance, egress whitelist test, KV perf baseline).

Marissa Cole
Technical Program Manager, Deployments
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Private VPC: 'Tether Meshlet' topology and cross-plane alignment review

Thanks, Kimberly / team — good set of artifacts. Nexa can support the hybrid approach (C) for the pilot. A few confirmations from our side: 

- Outbound ranges: we can provide a /24 block per region for the egress relay (will send exact ranges in a follow-up). FQDN allowlisting is acceptable for customers that cannot consume IP lists.
- MTU: 1500 required end-to-end; we can assist with an MTU probe during onboarding.
- Cert flows: 15m rotation is fine; we prefer short-lived certs but will accept 10-30m windows as discussed.

We can join a 30m sync tomorrow at either 09:00 PST or 13:30 PST — we'll be available both times. For the preflight, we request: a simple script to validate MTU, ability to fetch a short-lived cert, and an egress probe that retrieves https://nexa-healthcheck/internal.

We'll also create a runbook PR with our expected IP ranges and a short checklist.

Best,

Daniel Kim
Site Reliability Lead, NexaCloud Ops
daniel.kim@nexacloud.com
